domain_setting: A contemporary job search and recruitment process, from vacancy discovery and application documents through screening, interviews, and workplace skills.
recurring_scale_anchors: adult job seekers and recruiters are busts centered near x=152, with heads around y=55..90
application desks and interview tables sit around y=132..145, leaving floor visible below y=154
résumé pages, blank application forms, folders, laptops, calendars, portfolios, and interview chairs recur as props
all essential silhouettes stay within x=24..280 and y=16..176 on a 304x192 stage

polysemy_resolution_table.application: a candidate's request for a job; not software, an applied rule, or use of a substance
polysemy_resolution_table.application form / fill out a form: the document used to provide candidate information and the act of completing its blank fields; distinguish object from writing action
polysemy_resolution_table.apply for a job: submit a job-seeking request to an employer, from the Finding and applying group; not apply a rule or material
polysemy_resolution_table.job ad / job posting: a vacancy announcement; distinguish a general advertised notice from a structured employer listing on an online board
polysemy_resolution_table.jobs: a range of different work roles or openings, not one person's to-do tasks
polysemy_resolution_table.recruitment agency: a business intermediary matching job seekers with employers, not a government agency or a hiring employer itself
polysemy_resolution_table.volunteer: offer one's time or work without pay, selected by the job-search and work context; not merely a person called a volunteer on a form
polysemy_resolution_table.background check: verification of a candidate's identity and history during hiring; not background scenery or a criminal interrogation
polysemy_resolution_table.career summary / personal statement / co: distinct application materials: compact career overview, first-person profile, addressed explanatory letter, and structured work-history résumé; resume means the CV noun here, not restart
polysemy_resolution_table.education / experience / trained in / in: distinct qualifications: formal learning, prior work practice, specific instruction, deep understanding, demonstrated high competence, broad capabilities, and the most job-relevant capabilities
polysemy_resolution_table.interests: personal or professional topics a candidate enjoys, not ownership stakes
polysemy_resolution_table.portfolio: a curated collection of work samples, not a briefcase or bag despite the Japanese gloss
polysemy_resolution_table.professional achievements / proven track: specific completed accomplishments versus a sustained history of reliable results
polysemy_resolution_table.reference / references (employer): a person or statement that can verify an applicant's work suitability; not mentioning or referring to something
polysemy_resolution_table.availability: the times or date a candidate can work or attend an interview; not usefulness or product availability
polysemy_resolution_table.have an interview / interview: participate in a job interview versus the interview meeting itself; both selected by the hiring group rather than journalism or casual conversation
polysemy_resolution_table.manager: a workplace supervisor or hiring manager responsible for a team; not a sports manager or company owner by default
polysemy_resolution_table.salary expectations: the pay range a candidate hopes for, discussed professionally; not a payslip showing a salary already earned
polysemy_resolution_table.collaborate / coordinate / negotiate / o: work jointly toward a shared result, align moving parts and schedules, reach terms through discussion, and arrange tasks or materials respectively; coordinate is the verb, not the adjective meaning equal rank
polysemy_resolution_table.responsible for: having ownership or duty for a particular task or outcome
polysemy_resolution_table.service-oriented: attentive to helping and responding to customers, not a machine or industry category
polysemy_resolution_table.supervise: oversee a team's work and provide guidance, not perform every task personally

sibling_contrasts.job-finding process: job ad is a general notice; job posting is a structured listing; application is the request; application form is its blank document; fill out a form shows completion; apply for a job shows the submission action.
sibling_contrasts.application materials: career summary is concise work-history overview; personal statement is candidate's self-description; cover letter is addressed correspondence; résumé is a structured CV; portfolio is a set of work samples.
sibling_contrasts.qualifications: education is formal study; experience is prior practice; trained in signals instruction; in-depth knowledge is depth of understanding; proficient in is a high competence level; skills and key skills show broad versus role-critical capabilities.
sibling_contrasts.evidence and verification: professional achievements are concrete wins; proven track record is repeated success over time; reference is an external verifier; background check verifies identity/history.
sibling_contrasts.interview and employment conditions: availability is open schedule; salary expectations is desired compensation; have an interview shows a candidate participating; interview is the event; manager is the role on the employer side.
sibling_contrasts.work behaviors: collaborate is shared effort; coordinate aligns timing and resources; negotiate resolves terms; organize structures materials and tasks; responsible for shows ownership; service-oriented emphasizes customer care; supervise provides oversight.

art_direction: Editorial job-search scenes with warm paper, navy ink, blue application furniture, and restrained green/gold qualification marks. Use blank forms and icon-only document marks, no readable text, letters, numerals, logos, employer names, or real personal data. Make every document and workplace action compositionally distinct.
